A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of GRAPES, including equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–F. Their contents can be matched despite substantial rewriting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification experiments on eight datasets, with F1 scores, memory measurements, sample-size sensitivity, entropy diagnostics, and statistical analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments on twelve datasets, comparing GRAPES-RL and GRAPES-GFN with baselines, alongside memory, sensitivity, and entropy results.

M1.justification: V2 adds GRAPES-RL with a REINFORCE objective and replaces v1's shared scalar GFlowNet normalizer with a target-conditioned GCN (Section 4.3; Appendix F.3). Algorithm 1 changes layer construction from accumulating previously sampled nodes to combining the current sample with the target batch. Section 3 also changes the stated GCN normalization from row normalization to symmetric degree normalization.

E1.justification: V2 retains the eight original benchmarks and adds DBLP, BlogCat, ogbn-proteins, and snap-patents. These expand multi-label classification, featureless-graph evaluation, and protein and patent domains. Heterophily and multi-label classification are expanded rather than entirely new: v1 already evaluates Flickr and Yelp.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 add a uniform Random baseline, providing a direct control for whether learning the sampling policy helps. V2 also compares GRAPES-RL against GRAPES-GFN. All five existing named baselines remain, but Appendix B.2 reports a revised GraphSAINT variant for the main comparisons.

E3.justification: V1 takes baseline learning rates from their original papers; v2 states that learning rates are optimized on validation data for every method. V2 reports depth-two GraphSAINT random-walk sampling for the main benchmarks and node sampling for Figure 3, whereas v1 specifies node sampling throughout; residual contradictory wording leaves implementation details unclear. Added datasets introduce three-split BlogCat evaluation and ten random splits for DBLP and snap-patents.

E4.justification: Figure 3 reduces sample-size sensitivity coverage from eight datasets to Reddit, Flickr, Yelp, and ogbn-arxiv, while adding Random and separate RL/GFN comparisons. Entropy diagnostics expand to the four added datasets. V1's quantitative chi-square robustness analysis and accompanying rank analysis in Appendix D are removed, rather than relocated.

E5.justification: V2 removes v1's Friedman and Nemenyi testing, adjusted pairwise p-values, and robustness-rank significance analysis. Ten-run means and standard deviations remain in the main tables, and Figure 3 retains five repeats with 95% confidence intervals. Appendix C adds split-averaging information for new datasets; this does not establish increased run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The classification tables extensively replace scores and add results for Random, GRAPES-RL, and four datasets. For example, v1 reports GRAPES at 73.65 ± 0.21 on ogbn-products; v2 reports GRAPES-GFN at 70.66 ± 0.30, while AS-GCN changes from OOM to 73.94 ± 0.40. These are replacement results under revised methods/settings, not controlled performance changes. V1's GRAPES-32 accuracy table and rank/chi-square entries disappear; Figure 2's memory plot is retained.

T1.justification: Beyond moving the existing trajectory-balance material to Appendix F, v2 introduces the REINFORCE formulation and an unbiasedness assertion, formalizes conditioning the sampling distribution on cardinality in Appendix A, and replaces the constant-normalizer assumption. These alter the mathematical account of training. The new unbiasedness assertion is not reconciled with the explicitly off-policy estimator.

C1.justification: The contribution broadens from a GFlowNet sampler to an RL/GFN sampling framework. V1's general superiority claim becomes competitive overall performance with particular benefits on heterophilous, multi-label graphs. Random sampling matching sophisticated methods on some homophilous graphs becomes a central finding, and v2 newly claims a first rigorous twelve-dataset comparison. Memory-efficiency and low-sample-size claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets adaptive sampling through heterophily and multi-label complexity, acknowledges that Random can suffice on simpler graphs, and discusses GFlowNet diversity versus RL optimization. Section 6 removes the constant-normalizer limitation following the model revision, and adds limitations concerning evaluation on a fixed GCN architecture/depth and insufficient understanding of sampled subgraphs.

D1.justification: V2 specifies layer-indicator encoding, per-dataset epoch schedules, and learned embedding dimensions for featureless datasets. Appendix B adds A4000/A100 hardware and an estimated 200 compute days. The repository link, Adam optimizer, and search ranges remain. V1's explicit statement that test evaluation uses the full graph is omitted, without establishing an actual testing change.

R1.justification: Section 2 changes PASS's characterization from variance-focused to task-adaptive, distinguishing its feature-similarity policy from GRAPES's use of graph structure. V2 adds SubMix, DSKReG, graph-signal sampling, graphon transfer, and heterophily literature, substantially broadening its positioning. Statistical-method references disappear with the removed analyses; GFlowNet related work largely moves to Appendix F.1.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method exposition, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around general adaptive sampling and heterophily. GRAPES is renamed from GFlowNet Graph Neighbor Sampling to Graph Adaptive Sampling. Detailed GFlowNet background, loss derivation, and reward scaling move into Appendix F, while other appendices are reordered or replaced.

P2.justification: The main tables are redesigned around homophilous versus heterophilous datasets, with task and homophily rows. V2 adds a prior-work settings table and removes the rank, significance, and chi-square tables. Figure 3 changes from eight panels to four with revised axes and legends; entropy figures replace separate deviation panels with shaded bands and add datasets. The title/author layout and figure placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical interpretability through Random and RL/GFN controls, broader graph coverage, validation tuning for all baselines, and more qualified claims. However, v1 explicitly avoided REINFORCE because of the off-policy importance-weighting problem; v2 calls its new uncorrected off-policy estimator unbiased without resolving that issue (Section 4.3; Appendix A). V2 also removes statistical comparisons and part of the robustness evidence. These benefits and unresolved methodological concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
